resources.string: What Insert types. Hold a format on the panel to make it the default.
The map that a shared link opens
geo: link, opens the reader\'s own maps app
A WM Keyboard page with a button for every map
How much of your position a share gives away

A coarser precision moves the point to the centre of a fixed square of that size. The square is the same each time, so many shares from one place cannot be averaged back to that place. The address, the link and the Plus code all use the moved point.
Show a street and a city, not only numbers

The keyboard sends the point, at the precision you chose, to the address server one time for each share. The default server is Nominatim from OpenStreetMap. Off, nothing about your position leaves the phone until you send the text yourself.
If Android already allows it. Off, the panel waits for Locate me.
Words in braces are replaced: %1$s. A word with nothing to put in its place disappears.
Insert a saved place from the Places tab. It needs no location access and no network.
Search for it, use where you are, or type the coordinates
Read only when you tap Locate me or Use my location. Never in the background.
This build does not ask for location. Saved places still work.
Both use the location tool: its precision, its address lookup and its format. The first photo with either asks Android for location access.
A band along the bottom with the address, coordinates, time and Plus code. The pin on the viewfinder turns this on and off.
Send puts the place in the text box too, in the location tool\'s default format
The text goes in first, then the photo. Many chat apps use the text in the box as the photo\'s caption; others send it as a message of its own.
